candidates: Mode3 records some storage-path errors into the legacy histogram and some legacy durations into the storage histogram, causing misleading metrics
Mode3 records storage durations with the object name in the metric's kind label instead of the actual kind, causing potential Prometheus label-cardinality blowups

Mode3 passes the original UpdatedObjectInfo to legacy Update after unified Update succeeds, which can compute a different updated object against legacy's old state than what was actually persisted in unified storage, causing divergence
Mode3 returns immediately on any unified delete error including NotFound, so it won't attempt legacy cleanup when the object is missing in unified but present in legacy, leaving stale legacy data
Mode3 unit tests don't set mock expectations for async legacy calls (Delete/DeleteCollection) causing test failures with unexpected mock calls
Mode3 Create error-case test sets a Legacy expectation even though Storage.Create is called first, causing test failures
SetDualWritingMode defaults to Mode1 for an unset KV key and only transitions between Mode1 and Mode2, so Mode3 cannot be activated through configuration on a fresh KV store
Async legacy writes derive their timeout context from the incoming request context, so when the request finishes and cancels ctx, the legacy write can be cancelled immediately despite the 10s timeout
